summary: Day 1 of the 5-session grading window went the way the risk-off call predicted, but only by a small amount. SPY marked 757.12 at the close against the 759.81 reference (about -0.35%; VOO -0.29%, VTI -0.42% on the day), so it is still 3.9% above the 728.65 200-day and needs roughly another 0.65% fall over the next four sessions for the call to grade right. The cross-asset reads held. Duration again failed as a hedge (IEF -0.84%, BND -0.62% on the day, both now NEAR their stops at +0.8% and +0.9%). The rate-exposed VNQ fell 0.60%, in line with the hold-not-add downgrade. The favored Consumer Staples held up (DPZ +1.42%, KR +0.46%, WMT +0.31%). Health Care, the other favored sector, was soft but small (IDXX -0.65%, INCY -0.47%).
update: Keep risk-off at about 0.45 confidence. One session confirms direction but not size, and the 20-day vol of 22.6% makes a move of more than 1% over 5 sessions likely in either direction. The bonds-as-unreliable-hedge view is getting stronger. With IEF and BND both within 1% of their stops, the PM should expect duration to keep tracking equities lower, not offset them, while the Dec 9 25bp-vs-50bp debate is live. Signals to move back toward neutral: SPY's 5-day return turning positive while VIXY's 5-day move turns negative, TLT/IEF 5-day returns stabilizing, or UUP's rise reversing. A widening slide in HYG and LQD, or SPY approaching the 728.65 200-day, would raise confidence in risk-off. Track record: graded 8 of 12, which only matches the always-neutral baseline (0.667), so this risk-off call is the kind that has to pay off for the record to add value. No lesson in learning.json applies to the Market Analyst, so none shaped this review.
